newsitem.title: UK: Regan given time to prepare defence in CWS action.
newsitem.headline: Regan given time to prepare defence in CWS action.

text.p: Entrepreneur Andrew Regan's lawyers were on Wednesday given an extra three weeks to prepare their defence against a private prosecution brought against him by Britain's Co-operative Wholesale Society (CWS).

A preliminary hearing of the private case brought by the Co-op against Regan -- who last month failed in his 1.2 billion pounds ($2 billion) bid for the mutually-owned supermarkets-to-funeral parlours group -- was adjourned until June 18.
The CWS case against Regan, along with his business partner David Lyons, is for allegedly "aiding, abetting, counselling or procuring the theft and for handling stolen property".
Neither Regan or Lyons appeared in court but the Lord Mayor of London Roger Cork -- who was sitting in the City of London Magistrates Court -- said both should be present at the next hearing.
Allan Green, a former senior executive with CWS, is accused by his former employer of theft of confidential documents. Cork said he should also attend court at the next hearing.

Roy Amlot, the barrister representing the CWS, said he did not oppose the application to adjourn the case, but added that from the Co-op's point of view, the sooner a decision was made on the form of the trial the better.

Ian Burton, Regan's lawyer, said "The only thing Andrew Regan is guilty of is attempting to put a proposal to the members of the CWS. This legal action amounts to a malicious personal vendetta by Mr Melmoth".
A spokesman for both Regan and Lyons told Reuters they "still have every intention of defending this vigorously". ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
